newsitem.title: USA: Clear weather allows Missouri corn, soy harvesting.
newsitem.headline: Clear weather allows Missouri corn, soy harvesting.

text.p: A third consecutive week of mostly dry weather during the week ended Sunday allowed Missouri farmers to harvest fall crops and plant winter wheat, the Missouri Agriculture Statistics Service said.

Soybeans were 46 percent harvested versus 52 a year ago and the 52 percent average. Seventy-six percent were mature versus 82 a year ago and 86 average. The crop was rated 12 percent excellent, 51 good, 30 fair, six percent poor and one very poor.
Corn was 62 percent harvested, ahead of 54 a year ago and the 61 average. Nearly all of the crop in the southern third of the state had been harvested.
Sorghum was 58 percent harvested versus 58 a year ago and the 61 average.
Winter wheat was 51 percent planted and 24 percent was emerged versus 60 and 26 percent, respectively, a year ago and the 52 and 27 averages.
Cotton was 62 percent harvested compared with 58 percent a year ago and the 62 average.
Topsoil moisture was rated two percent surplus, 72 percent adequate, 24 short and two very short.
